summary: Narrowed the asserted defect claim back to unresolved after re-deriving the propose-time guard against the decoded history, because the derivation contradicts the trigger the claim relied on. What the receipts support stays on record: a joint-enter change that alters no membership still creates a joint configuration (index 17), the leave-joint entry needed to exit it is proposed only by a node that is leader when it applies the change, the decoded history contains two joint-enter changes and no leave, three nodes applied that history in order with reapplied_entry false and batch bounds at applied_before+1 or their first entry, and the second change is rejected with the Changer's 'config is already joint', which applyConfChange turns into a process-fatal panic. What no longer holds is my assertion that this history is reachable through the target's own proposal path: a leader's pendingConfIndex is the last index at its election plus whatever changes it appends, so while its applied index is below that, alreadyPending blocks any new configuration change; and if its applied index has reached the committed joint change, its tracker is joint and alreadyJoint blocks it. I could not construct any leader state that appends the second joint change - a later-elected leader inherits a pendingConfIndex covering the first change and a restarted node that later takes office resets to the same rule - so the decoded history should not have entered the log through stepLeader with DisableConfChangeValidation false, leaving either a path I have not identified or an artefact of the sweep's bookkeeping, with no observation to choose. Counterweight recorded honestly: the derivation is a source argument, not an observation, and the receipts themselves show the guard admitting changes in hand-built states, so the sweep could involve a state of that kind I have not enumerated; the harness rebuilds nodes at restart events and registers a node outside the configuration, so a bookkeeping path producing such a log is plausible; and violations=0 means no safety result is affected either way. The discriminator is concrete: record, whenever a configuration change is appended, the appending node's pendingConfIndex, applied index, tracker jointness and whether DisableConfChangeValidation is set, plus the entry type and term at every position in the rejected history - index 3 in particular, which the decoding still leaves unexplained.
